harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a root crontab entry on node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15, appending output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Verified the binary runs successfully and writes to the log. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, issued a native reboot, polled until the node came back, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified cron service, crontab entry, log contents, and binary all persisted post-restart.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: confirmed /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance exists and cron service is active on node1
Manually ran the binary via sudo shell redirect to confirm it executes and writes successfully to the log path used by cron
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline (cron active/enabled, crontab present, log present)
Issued native reboot on node1 via backgrounded sudo -n reboot so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until command execution was available again
Verified boot_id changed after restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: cron enabled/active, crontab entry intact, log content persisted, binary present

evidence.requirement: Cron job runs inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 and retains output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Baseline confirmed binary and cron service present; crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' installed for root and verified via crontab -l; manual execution via sudo shell confirmed the binary writes 'inventory maintenance completed at ...' into /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log using the same redirect path cron will use.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d), confirmed cron active, crontab entry present, and log content present.
Issued 'sudo -n reboot' backgrounded so the exec call returned 'reboot acknowledged and issued' before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable (connection refused) immediately after reboot, then came back with a new boot_id (794a4672-88bc-474c-8003-21b11e9c6af5), proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After restart, cron service is enabled and active, root crontab still contains the 02:15 inventory-maintenance entry, /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log content persisted, and the binary file is unchanged and present.
